items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: But there were still Buddy DeFranco and Tony Scott and a few other guys who were playing the clarinet and playing it bop, so I’ve been influenced by that

ctx.x: But you eventually — correct me if I’m wrong, please — but your tastes maybe worked backwards again?

Yeah, pretty much. I mean I spent a lot of time listening to Benny Goodman records, and becoming a clarinetist especially. What’s available to listen to, as opposed to because during the bop era, when bop became real popular, there weren’t too many clarinet players anymore. The clarinet players were Goodman and Shaw and those guys, the guys who led the big bands. But there are a lot more saxophone players because there were five saxophones in every big band, and usually only one clarinet player if any at all. So…
What was your classical training on the clarinet?
